title: Cap. X Arg. VIII close: Prosper — in infants neither prior merit nor future devotion is chosen; catholic sense: many die debtors of eternal death; Arminius rejected
pass_a_gloss: Prosper also everywhere embraces the same sentence: De lib. arbitr. ad Ruffin. In infants neither what precedes is chosen, nor future devotion. In the Epistle unto Augustine, Little ones, he says, as yet having no wills, no proper actions, are not without God’s judgment severed, when some through regeneration are taken up among the heirs of the heavenly kingdom, others without Baptism pass among the debtors of perpetual death. Finally that I may briefly finish, it was the constant sentence of the whole catholic Church (God’s secrets being always reserved unto him) that All infants are born guilty of eternal death, many not regenerated, and pass as debtors of eternal death, as we have received from Prosper. Arminius’s sentence therefore, which grants no reprobation except from the foreseen unbelief of the reprobate and perseverance in the same, was always rejected and condemned by the reckoning of the whole orthodox Church.
pass_b_english: Prosper everywhere holds the same (De libero arbitrio ad Ruffinum): In infants neither what precedes is chosen, nor future devotion. In his letter to Augustine: Little ones, he says, still having no wills and no acts of their own, are not parted without God’s judgment—some through regeneration taken up among heirs of the heavenly kingdom, others without baptism passing among debtors of perpetual death. In short, the whole catholic church’s constant sense (always reserving God’s secrets to him) has been: All infants are born debtors of eternal death; many pass unregenerate as debtors of eternal death—as we have it from Prosper. So Arminius’s view, which grants no reprobation except from the reprobate’s foreseen unbelief and perseverance in it, was always rejected and condemned by the whole orthodox church’s reckoning.
source_text: Prosper etiam eandem sententiam ubique amplectitur: De lib. arbitr. ad Ruffin. In infantibus nec praecedens eligitur, nec futura devotio. In Epistola ad Augustinum, Parvuli, inquit, nullas adhuc habentes voluntates, nullas proprias actiones, non sine Dei judicio secernuntur, cum alii per regenerationem inter caelestis regni assumantur heredes, alii sine Baptismo inter mortis perpetuae transeant debitores. Denique ut brevi absolvam, constans fuit totius Ecclesiae catholicae sententia, (reservatis semper Deo arcanis suis) Infantes omnes nasci reos mortis aeternae, multos non regeneratos, et transire debitores mortis aeternae, ut ex Prospero accepimus. Arminii igitur sententia, quae reprobationem nullam concedit nisi ex praevisa reprobatorum infidelitate et perseverantia in eadem, fuit semper totius Ecclesiae orthodoxae calculo rejecta et condemnata.
